<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 72a302a9dde3347e15a971c5da28df205496a217` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `535453a9c8c580a5aba191e2d5142bd6d2cb5b8d` — the merge of head `8ad60d9a9518ca6a65d48c4ce94397e40512cf97` into base `72a302a9dde3347e15a971c5da28df205496a217`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 535453a9c8c580a5aba191e2d5142bd6d2cb5b8d && git checkout 535453a9c8c580a5aba191e2d5142bd6d2cb5b8d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 72a302a9dde3347e15a971c5da28df205496a217 8ad60d9a9518ca6a65d48c4ce94397e40512cf97 && git checkout -B drift-repro 72a302a9dde3347e15a971c5da28df205496a217 && git merge --no-ff 8ad60d9a9518ca6a65d48c4ce94397e40512cf97

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 72a302a9dde3347e15a971c5da28df205496a217
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 72a302a9dde3347e15a971c5da28df205496a217` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8ad60d9a9518ca6a65d48c4ce94397e40512cf97`
Local-runs: none
Scope: the whole diff (15 files, +926 / -33, merge-base `ab488d9b7d`). Read to judge it: `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/unmanaged-tables.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/schema-migration-plugins.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/sql-driver.ts`, `packages/drivers/driver-turso/src/turso-driver.ts`, `packages/cli/src/index.ts`, `packages/cli/package.json`, `.github/workflows/upgrade-harness-optin.yml`.

The face is the declaration face: `check-governed-merges` reads 0 governed paths, nothing under `packages/spec/src/**`, and the PR body and changeset declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, not a narrowing. So the lane seat records it at `TIER_DEFAULT`. Inputs: the ruling 6328195425, the claim 6333411407, the dev report 6334476182, the PR body, the diff, and the head's check-runs. Nothing was built or run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

**Ruling item 2: the advisory lives in `os migrate plan`.** Executed as ruled.
- The section is computed at `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/plan.ts:283`, before the "in sync" return. An 18.0.0-born store has no drift and every such column, so the advisory has to come first.
- It is printed as its own block at `:433`, above the drift verdict.
- Under `--json` it is a separate key at `:334`. It is outside `total` and `changes`.
- No exit path moves: the only `this.exit` calls in the file are the pre-existing failure paths (`:234`, `:236`, `:517`, `:519`), and the diff adds none.
- No boot line: the diff touches no `serve` or boot file.
- No drift op: the differ's `ceremonyOwnedNullability` exemption is untouched, and the harness pins that no `nullability_mismatch` names `organization_id`.

**Population.**
- The tenant field per table comes from each planned driver's `tenantFieldByTable`, the same map `resolveTenantField` reads.
- `sys_sso_provider` (tenancy disabled) and undeclared tables are not listed. The harness pins that the only nullable `organization_id` tables left out on fixture-18.0.0 are exactly those two, `sys_notification_subscription` and `sys_sso_provider`, and that nothing is listed that is not nullable.
- A shard is read through `rotationBaseOf` (`nullable-tenant-columns.ts:219`).
- "Could not read" never reads as "none nullable":
  - a plan that did not compose the served object set is `unreadable` (`:202`);
  - so is an unreadable driver map, or a failed or missing catalog read;
  - `columns: []` is reserved for a read that found none.
- Identifiers are inlined only after the `SAFE_IDENTIFIER` filter (`:113`).
- The Postgres and MySQL forms use the same `ANY (current_schemas(false))` and `DATABASE()` idiom as `unmanaged-tables.ts:206` and `organization-ownership-plan.ts:616`. Only SQLite was measured; PG and MySQL are read from code.

**Residue marking against what the ceremony really does.** Each `leaves` reason in `ceremonyLeaves` (`:167`) is the same condition the ceremony applies:
- **Shard.** A nullable shard is `unsupported` in `applyNotNullThroughDrift` (`organization-ownership-not-null.ts:51`).
- **Transport.** It is the same `driftApplyLimit('tighten_not_null')` call (`:172` against `organization-ownership-not-null.ts:71`). The Turso remote face answers `needs-table-rebuild` for that op (`turso-driver.ts:684`).
- **`notNullExempt`.** The plan sets `willReceive: false` with that same reason (`organization-ownership-plan.ts:1123`).
- **`mirror-deletion`.** `willReceive: false` (`:1098`).
- **`column-drop` tables.** These are not in the population, because their objects carry no tenant field (inventory citations `systemFields.tenant: false`). This is judged from the citations plus the measured fixture: 61 `tightens` against the ceremony's measured `applied` 61. It was not checked table by table.

**Ruling item 4: the stale shard sentences and the shard outcome.**
- The old sentence ("each new shard is created … nullable") is gone. The driver claim that replaces it holds: `ensureShardTable` creates the base's tenant column NOT NULL (`sql-driver.ts:12225`, `name === baseTenantField`).
- `isNotNull` is asked of a shard only, on the shard's own database driver (`organization-ownership.ts:888`). An unreadable answer is `null` and falls back to `unsupported`, which is the conservative side.
- `already-not-null` is counted in `alreadyNotNull` (`organization-ownership-apply.ts:3728`, `:3747`). It adds no note and no blocker, and the step stays `done`. This is pinned by the new 5d case and by the harness leg (`alreadyNotNull` at least 1, and no "created … nullable" note).

**The `--json` widening.**
- The two key-set pins in `plan.apply-limit.test.ts` widen by exactly the one key, and every other assertion is unchanged.
- `NotNullOutcome` and the advisory types are not reachable from the CLI's `exports` map (`.`, `./console` and `./hook-body`; `src/index.ts` names neither). The widened union is CLI report output, not a published type.

**Tests.**
- No pre-existing assertion was weakened.
- The harness gains three legs on the 18.0.0 describe: plan before, after the voluntary ceremony, and a fresh store.
- `SERVED_ENV` is passed only by the new legs. `runOwnershipCeremony` and `runSchemaPlan` take an optional `env` with default `{}`, so the existing callers are unchanged.
- The dev's six ablations each turn a named pin red, judged structurally from the pins.

**Prose (cli.mdx, upgrading.mdx, changeset), sentence by sentence against the diff.**
- The section's text, remedy and placement match `renderNullableTenantColumns`. The example's indents match it too: the first line through `printInfo`, the bullets at 6 + 2 spaces, the last line at 6.
- "Turso remote: every listed column is one the ceremony leaves" matches the `driftApplyLimit` branch.
- "A fresh install … prints nothing" is pinned by the fresh-store leg.
- The JSON shapes match the types, except that the docs' `unreadable` shape omits its `adr` key. That is minor.
- One imprecision, not blocking: for an `attribution` or `report` table that still holds a NULL row the ceremony cannot attribute, the advisory says `tightens`, but the ceremony's plan says `willReceive: false`. The module doc states this limit (`nullable-tenant-columns.ts`, header). The section's last line and `upgrading.mdx` ("tightens them to NOT NULL when you run it") say it without the condition. The remedy line sends the operator to the ceremony's own `--out PLAN`, which names such a table, so nothing is hidden.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cli`: `patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`. Correct under the changeset gate: there is no protocol face, and the change is a widening (one added `--json` key, one added outcome value and summary count). No accepted input, refusal or exit code moves. Check Changeset is green on the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Clause-② re-declared `yes (widening)`** against the claim's expected `no`. Accepted, because the declaration is accurate. It is what puts this review on the declaration face at `TIER_DEFAULT`, and both the PR body and the changeset carry it.
- **`open_questions`:** none.
- **The out-of-scope finding** (a plan run without `OS_AUTH_SECRET` composes no auth family, so the advisory sees 52 of 63 on fixture-18.0.0). This is the whole plan's existing composition rule, not this PR's. The plan already says so in that case and names the remedy (`schema-migration-plugins.ts:2051-2057` on main: re-run with the secret). Nothing to file.
- **R2.** This PR changes the 18.x upgrade harness, and that lane is opt-in. It was skipped at open, so `needs:upgrade-harness` was applied, and the lane is running on this head. Landing waits on it, outside this verdict.
- **Nit, not blocking:** in `packages/qa/dogfood/test/upgrade-harness/ceremony.ts`, the new `NullableTenantColumn` interface was inserted between `runSchemaPlan`'s doc block and the function, so that doc now sits detached above the interface.

## Seat check

- **Shape:** the cli `os migrate plan` advisory (`utils/nullable-tenant-columns.ts`), the ceremony's `not-null` shard outcome, tests, the upgrade harness legs, `cli.mdx`, `upgrading.mdx`, and one changeset. 15 files, +926 / -33. `check-governed-merges --pr 25179`: 0 of 15 paths governed, so this is an ordinary queue landing.
- **What it does:**
  - `os migrate plan` lists every tenant column still nullable and names `os migrate organization-ownership` as the remedy. Each column says whether the ceremony tightens it or leaves it, and why.
  - The section is advisory only. It is not drift, proposes no op, does not count in `total`, and moves no exit code. Under `--json` it is the separate `nullableTenantColumns` field.
  - The ceremony now reports a rotation shard the driver created NOT NULL as `already-not-null` instead of `unsupported`, and the stale shard sentences are corrected.
  - No boot line, no shape-generation change, and no `docs/adr/**` or `releases/**` edit.
- **Review:** `TIER_DEFAULT`, declaration face. The dev re-declared `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, which is accurate: one `--json` key and one outcome value are added. **PASS** 6334904919 at this head.
- **R2:** this PR changes the 18.x upgrade harness, whose lane is opt-in. The seat applied `needs:upgrade-harness`. The lane ran on this head (job 119687975985) and passed 15/15, including the fixture-18.0.0 legs and the three new ones: plan before the ceremony, after it, and on a fresh store.
- **Measured (dev report):** fixture-18.0.0 lists 63 columns: 61 `tightens`, which equals the ceremony's measured `applied` 61, and 2 `leaves` (a pre-7b-0 shard and `sys_email_template`). After the ceremony, only those 2 are listed. A fresh store lists none. R1 and R4 boots are ready, with health 200.
- **CI:** 47 check runs on the head, none failing. The required checks (TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Governed Surface Queue Guard) succeeded, and Check Changeset is green. The skipped runs are opt-in lanes.
- **Not blocking, not filed:**
  - The advisory's `tightens` (and `upgrading.mdx`) does not carry the condition that a table still holding unattributable NULL rows stays nullable after the ceremony. The remedy line sends the operator to the ceremony's own `--out PLAN`, which names such a table.
  - A detached doc block in the harness helper `ceremony.ts`.
  - The no-secret composition gap is the plan's existing rule, and the plan already names its remedy.
- **Landing:** the seat flips the PR ready and enables auto-merge. `Fixes #25134` closes the card. The merge commit is then handed to #25154 for its last citation (B4 part 2, D1).
